subject: humanities
passage: Dastangoi, the Urdu art of telling long tales of adventure, flourished in northern India in the 1800s. A skilled dastango could hold an audience for hours with voice and gesture alone, improvising around a vast cycle of tales about the hero Amir Hamza. The last celebrated performer died in 1928, and the living tradition ended with him; no performance was ever recorded. What survived were the tales, printed in the late 1800s in an edition of tens of thousands of pages. When performers in Delhi revived the form in the mid-2000s, those volumes gave them the words but nothing of the manner; how a dastango paced a scene or shifted between voices had to be imagined anew. The revival is thus less a restoration than a fresh creation on an old text.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Because dastangoi's texts survived but its performance style did not, the revival had to reinvent how the tales are told.
choices.B: The stories of Amir Hamza were preserved only because a performer recorded them before 1928.
choices.C: Dastangoi performers of the 1800s could hold audiences for hours using only their voices and gestures.
choices.D: Modern performers have faithfully reconstructed dastangoi from descriptions left by nineteenth-century audiences.

explanation.why: The text contrasts what was lost (the living tradition, with "no recording of a performance") and what survived (the printed tales). The revival therefore had "the words but nothing of the manner," so the performance style "had to be imagined anew." The last sentence states the conclusion: the revival is "a fresh creation built on an old text."
explanation.A: Correct. This captures both halves of the contrast and the conclusion that the revival had to reinvent the manner of performance.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reverses the text, which says no recording was ever made; the stories survived in print.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is a detail about the old performers, not the point of the text, which is about the revival.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never mentions descriptions by audiences, and it says the revival is not a restoration.
